implementation: Compiler registry prefixes use an explicit fallible hash callback for the AIR fingerprint while retaining exact metadata, field ordering, domains, compiler programs and witness encodings
A private prepared registry prefix is bound to height and key count and forwarded through all supported wrapper, pair, empty, merge, finalizer and registration-template compiler paths

Recursive session compilation and all five registration APIs use scoped selected-backend hashing with policy and worker admission before metadata or hash work; GPU errors propagate without CPU fallback
Public CPU compiler and geometry APIs, registry profile approval, and independent CPU proof verification remain reference paths
Registry compilation reports actual completed Preprocessing GPU hash batches and event time, including completed work before failure; full capability coverage remains incomplete
Existing witness reservations include the fixed 32800-byte public hash scratch; no new runtime switch, cached prefix or remote device handles are introduced
limitations: Integration proofs are bounded recursive empty proofs at height 2048, not full-size wrapped-wallet, merged, finalized or mixed-transaction root proofs
Root conformance covers all transaction kinds, ordered dense prefixes, padding, context binding, metadata rejection and finalizer derivation; this is not a full transaction-throughput measurement
Compiler constant arithmetic (domain generators, periodic inputs and quotient coset normalization), individual remaining stage observations and strict GPU admission are unfinished
Wallet/batch and C-ABI proving arithmetic, unsupported legacy/profile arithmetic, AMD/Metal qualification, full-size memory, cancellation/retry and sustained pool throughput remain open
